mn143:2.12: “Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
mn143:2.13: He bows with his head to your feet.”
mn143:2.14: Then he went to Venerable Sāriputta, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,
mn143:2.15: “Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
mn143:2.16: He bows with his head to your feet,
mn143:2.18: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”
mn143:4.3: I’m not keeping well, Honorable Sāriputta, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

mn143:19.2: “Mendicants, last night, late at night, a certain glorious godling, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to me, bowed, and stood to one side.
mn143:19.3: Standing to one side, that godling addressed me in verse:
mn143:19.5: frequented by the Saṅgha of seers,
mn143:19.6: where the King of Dhamma stayed:
mn143:19.15: that’s how they become purified in that.
mn143:19.18: Even a mendicant who has crossed over
mn143:19.20: Mendicants, that is what that godling said.
mn143:19.21: Knowing that the Teacher concurred, he bowed to me and respectfully circled me, keeping me on his right, before vanishing right there.”
mn143:20.9: Advice to Anāthapiṇḍika is finished—the first.
